asc.plainEnglish: The component owns activate, cost, and cooldown.
asc.whyGame: Cost and cooldown stay on the ability system.

expansions.title: The ability system as a door
expansions.detail: If the ability system is a use, the hit calls one interface. A door, a switch, and a pickup can share it without a new cast.

expansions.title: The ability system as data
expansions.detail: Designer numbers for the ability system live on a row. a one second timer that broadcasts OnEffect, which is the fear or cost reaction reads the row instead of a literal.

expansions.title: The ability system as a listener
expansions.detail: Later systems listen for ApplyEffect. They do not broadcasting OnEffect from Tick, or also subtracting the cost by hand.

quiz.prompt: Who checks an ability's cost before it commits?
choices: The ability system component on the character.
The character class, in its Tick.
The widget that draws the stamina bar.
Whoever pressed the button, before the ability system is asked.
quiz.why: The component owns activate, cost, and cooldown.
quiz.review_prompt: Who checks an ability's cost before it commits?

quiz.prompt: A designer puts the cooldown test on the character Tick so it never misses a frame. What breaks?
choices: The character is doing the ability system's job
No separate clock, if a cooldown could only live on the frame loop.
The ability system refuses to start if Tick is also checking.
OnRep of health starts the ability instead.
quiz.why: Cost and cooldown stay on the ability system.
quiz.review_prompt: A designer puts the cooldown test on the character Tick so it never misses a frame. What breaks?

quiz.prompt: True or false: The ability system component owns activate, cost, and cooldown. The character does not.
choices: True
False
quiz.why: That is the whole lesson.
quiz.review_prompt: True or false: The ability system component owns activate, cost, and cooldown. The character does not.

quiz.prompt: Cost and cooldown stay on the ability system, not copied into each character's Tick.
choices: True
False
quiz.why: The component already owns that check.
quiz.review_prompt: True or false: Each new character class should copy the cost check into its own Tick.

quiz.prompt: A rifle and a medic both spend stamina. Where does that shared check live?
choices: On the ability system component both characters already have.
In each character's constructor, as a different float.
On the HUD, which subtracts stamina when it redraws.
In the player controller's input function, before any ability exists.
quiz.why: One component, many characters.
quiz.review_prompt: A rifle and a medic both spend stamina. Where does that shared check live?

quiz.prompt: What is the character allowed to do when the player presses the ability button?
choices: Ask the ability system to activate. It does not decide the cost.
Subtract the cost itself and then tell the system the ability already ran.
Start a Tick that polls the button for the rest of the match.
Write the cooldown onto a replicated mesh pointer.
quiz.why: The character asks. The system decides.
quiz.review_prompt: What is the character allowed to do when the player presses the ability button?

quiz.prompt: True or false: Two characters can share one ability system component type and still have different abilities granted to them.
choices: True
False
quiz.why: The component is the owner. The grants differ.
quiz.review_prompt: True or false: Two characters can share one ability system component type and still have different abilities granted to them.

quiz.prompt: A cooldown is checked in the character and again in the ability system. What does the player see?
choices: The ability can be blocked twice, or the two checks can disagree.
A faster cooldown, because two checks finish sooner.
The widget hides, because cooldowns are visual only.
The server ignores both and activates anyway.
quiz.why: One owner, one check.
quiz.review_prompt: A cooldown is checked in the character and again in the ability system. What does the player see?

quiz.prompt: True or false: The HUD should subtract stamina when it draws the bar, so the ability system can stay empty.
choices: True
False
quiz.why: The bar reads the value. It does not spend it.
quiz.review_prompt: True or false: The HUD should subtract stamina when it draws the bar, so the ability system can stay empty.

quiz.prompt: Where does a new ability get told it may start?
choices: The ability system, after cost and tags pass.
Once at startup, for every ability the character might ever have.
The overlap of a nearby pickup.
OnRep of an unrelated health float.
quiz.why: Activate is a system call.
quiz.review_prompt: Where does a new ability get told it may start?

quiz.prompt: True or false: Deleting the ability system and inlining its checks into every character is how you keep costs consistent.
choices: True
False
quiz.why: Inlining is how the checks drift apart.
quiz.review_prompt: True or false: Deleting the ability system and inlining its checks into every character is how you keep costs consistent.

quiz.prompt: A client predicts the ability started. Who still has to accept the cost?
choices: The authority's ability system. The client's guess is not the commit.
The client alone, because prediction already played the animation.
The health bar, on its next paint.
No one. Costs are cosmetic.
quiz.why: Prediction can show. The system still commits.
quiz.review_prompt: A client predicts the ability started. Who still has to accept the cost?

attributes.plainEnglish: One number, on the attribute set.
attributes.whyGame: Do not keep a second health float.

expansions.title: Attributes as a door
expansions.detail: If attributes is a use, the hit calls one interface. A door, a switch, and a pickup can share it without a new cast.

expansions.title: Attributes as data
expansions.detail: Designer numbers for attributes live on a row. a one second timer that broadcasts OnEffect, which is the fear or cost reaction reads the row instead of a literal.

expansions.title: Attributes as a listener
expansions.detail: Later systems listen for ApplyEffect. They do not broadcasting OnEffect from Tick, or also subtracting the cost by hand.

quiz.prompt: Where does GAS health live?
choices: On an attribute set the ability system can change.
In a second float on the character, next to the attribute.
Only inside the health bar's text.
In the mesh component, replicated as a transform.
quiz.why: One number, on the attribute set.
quiz.review_prompt: Where does GAS health live?

quiz.prompt: A programmer keeps Character.Health and an attribute named Health. A heal updates only the attribute. What does the HUD show if it reads the character float?
choices: The old value. The two numbers have diverged.
The attribute, because Unreal copies it across automatically.
A literal zero, if a second float were illegal.
The mesh bounds, because health is a transform.
quiz.why: Do not keep a second health float.
quiz.review_prompt: A programmer keeps Character.Health and an attribute named Health. A heal updates only the attribute. What does the HUD show if it reads the character float?

quiz.prompt: True or false: Health as an attribute is one number the ability system can change. Do not keep a second health float.
choices: True
False
quiz.why: That is the lesson.
quiz.review_prompt: True or false: Health as an attribute is one number the ability system can change. Do not keep a second health float.

quiz.prompt: True or false: A second health float is useful so the HUD can disagree with the ability system on purpose.
choices: True
False
quiz.why: Disagreement is the bug.
quiz.review_prompt: True or false: A second health float is useful so the HUD can disagree with the ability system on purpose.

quiz.prompt: A damage effect should change which number?
choices: The health attribute, through the ability system.
A local float the character subtracts in Tick.
The widget's cached text.
The actor's location Z, as a clever encoding.
quiz.why: Effects write attributes.
quiz.review_prompt: A damage effect should change which number?

quiz.prompt: Who is allowed to be the source of truth for that attribute in a multiplayer game?
choices: The authority's ability system. Clients receive the result.
Each machine, so the hit feels instant and the server guesses later.
The UI on the owning client only.
The projectile, which stores health for the victim.
quiz.why: The system on the authority owns the attribute.
quiz.review_prompt: Who is allowed to be the source of truth for that attribute in a multiplayer game?

quiz.prompt: True or false: An attribute set can hold health, stamina, and ammo as separate attributes without a parallel set of raw floats.
choices: True
False
quiz.why: The set is the list of numbers.
quiz.review_prompt: True or false: An attribute set can hold health, stamina, and ammo as separate attributes without a parallel set of raw floats.

quiz.prompt: A save writes the raw character float and ignores the attribute. What loads?
choices: A health the ability system is no longer using.
Both copies, if they were the same memory.
The mesh, because attributes serialize as transforms.
No attribute, if attributes could not be saved at all.
quiz.why: Save the attribute value, not a shadow float.
quiz.review_prompt: A save writes the raw character float and ignores the attribute. What loads?

quiz.prompt: True or false: The widget should own a third copy of health so animations can read it faster.
choices: True
False
quiz.why: The widget reads. It does not own.
quiz.review_prompt: True or false: The widget should own a third copy of health so animations can read it faster.

quiz.prompt: A buff adds 20 health. Where is the addition expressed?
choices: In a gameplay effect that modifies the health attribute.
In the character Tick, which adds 20 whenever the buff tag might be on.
In the HUD paint, which draws a higher number without changing the attribute.
In the damage type class constructor.
quiz.why: Effects modify attributes.
quiz.review_prompt: A buff adds 20 health. Where is the addition expressed?

quiz.prompt: True or false: Keeping the old float 'just in case' is safe as long as you remember to update it in most paths.
choices: True
False
quiz.why: The path you forget is the desync.
quiz.review_prompt: True or false: Keeping the old float 'just in case' is safe as long as you remember to update it in most paths.

quiz.prompt: What does the player notice when only the attribute changes and the HUD still reads the old float?
choices: The bar lies. The character can be dead while the bar looks full, or the reverse.
No binding, if the bar read the attribute by magic.
The ability system shuts down.
Input stops.
quiz.why: One number, one reader.
quiz.review_prompt: What does the player notice when only the attribute changes and the HUD still reads the old float?

activate.whyGame: The tag is the handle. The system finds the ability.

expansions.title: Activate by tag as a door
expansions.detail: If activate by tag is a use, the hit calls one interface. A door, a switch, and a pickup can share it without a new cast.

expansions.title: Activate by tag as data
expansions.detail: Designer numbers for activate by tag live on a row. a one second timer that broadcasts OnEffect, which is the fear or cost reaction reads the row instead of a literal.

expansions.title: Activate by tag as a listener
expansions.detail: Later systems listen for ApplyEffect. They do not broadcasting OnEffect from Tick, or also subtracting the cost by hand.

quiz.prompt: How does this course start an ability?
choices: By gameplay tag, so a new ability does not need a new cast.
By casting to each ability Blueprint from the character.
By trying every ability on each frame.
By OnRep of health, which is assumed to mean 'pressed the button'.
quiz.why: Activate by tag.
quiz.review_prompt: How does this course start an ability?

quiz.prompt: A new dash ability is added. What code change does a tag activation avoid?
choices: A new cast, or a new branch, inside the character.
No lookup, if you still cast to every ability class.
A new Tick function per ability.
A new replicated mesh for the dash.
quiz.why: The tag is the handle. The system finds the ability.
quiz.review_prompt: A new dash ability is added. What code change does a tag activation avoid?

quiz.prompt: True or false: Activate by gameplay tag so a new ability does not need a new cast.
choices: True
False
quiz.why: That is the lesson.
quiz.review_prompt: True or false: Activate by gameplay tag so a new ability does not need a new cast.

quiz.prompt: True or false: Each ability should be started with its own Cast node on the character so the graph shows every class.
choices: True
False
quiz.why: That cast list is what the tag avoids.
quiz.review_prompt: True or false: Each ability should be started with its own Cast node on the character so the graph shows every class.

quiz.prompt: The button for reload is pressed. What does input call?
choices: Activate by the reload tag. The ability system finds the granted ability.
A cast to the reload Blueprint, written into the input function.
Set Magazine directly, skipping the ability so cost cannot block it.
The health notify, if reload were a replication event.
quiz.why: Input asks. The system activates.
quiz.review_prompt: The button for reload is pressed. What does input call?

quiz.prompt: A stun tag is on. What can block the reload ability without a special case in the character?
choices: The ability system, because the tag activation can fail its tag check.
No failure, if a tag could not fail to activate.
The button art, by refusing to draw.
Deleting the ability on each frame.
quiz.why: Tags are how the system says no.
quiz.review_prompt: A stun tag is on. What can block the reload ability without a special case in the character?

quiz.prompt: True or false: Two weapons can grant different abilities under the same input tag, and the character function does not change.
choices: True
False
quiz.why: The grant changes. The activate call does not.
quiz.review_prompt: True or false: Two weapons can grant different abilities under the same input tag, and the character function does not change.

quiz.prompt: Someone activates by class with a hard cast 'so it is explicit'. What grows when the tenth ability arrives?
choices: The cast list, and every character that copied it.
No cost, if a cast named no class.
The attribute set, which must add a float per cast.
The fog system, which traces for each cast.
quiz.why: Tags stay one call.
quiz.review_prompt: Someone activates by class with a hard cast 'so it is explicit'. What grows when the tenth ability arrives?

quiz.prompt: True or false: Begin Play should activate every ability once so they are 'warmed up'.
choices: True
False
quiz.why: Activate means start. Begin Play would fire them all at spawn.
quiz.review_prompt: True or false: Begin Play should activate every ability once so they are 'warmed up'.

quiz.prompt: Where does the cost get a chance to refuse the tag activation?
choices: Inside the ability system, before the ability commits.
After the montage has finished, when it is too late to refuse.
On the client only, with the server forced to accept.
In the damage number popup.
quiz.why: Cost runs as part of activation.
quiz.review_prompt: Where does the cost get a chance to refuse the tag activation?

quiz.prompt: True or false: A gameplay tag is just a comment. The real start is still a chain of casts.
choices: True
False
quiz.why: The tag is the lookup.
quiz.review_prompt: True or false: A gameplay tag is just a comment. The real start is still a chain of casts.

quiz.prompt: What does the player see if the tag is misspelled and nothing is granted under it?
choices: The button does nothing. No cast error lists the missing class, because there is no cast.
Every ability fires, because a bad tag means all tags.
Health drops to zero.
The character Tick takes over and runs the ability by name.
quiz.why: A missing grant is a quiet no.
quiz.review_prompt: What does the player see if the tag is misspelled and nothing is granted under it?

effects.plainEnglish: The effect is the cost and the cooldown.

expansions.title: Effects as a door
expansions.detail: If effects is a use, the hit calls one interface. A door, a switch, and a pickup can share it without a new cast.

expansions.title: Effects as data
expansions.detail: Designer numbers for effects live on a row. a one second timer that broadcasts OnEffect, which is the fear or cost reaction reads the row instead of a literal.

expansions.title: Effects as a listener
expansions.detail: Later systems listen for ApplyEffect. They do not broadcasting OnEffect from Tick, or also subtracting the cost by hand.

quiz.prompt: What applies the cooldown and the cost?
choices: A gameplay effect. Do not also subtract the cost by hand.
The character Tick, subtracting a float and setting a timer of its own.
The fade, when the bar finishes animating.
The notify, which would play the flash and spend the cost again.
quiz.why: The effect is the cost and the cooldown.
quiz.review_prompt: What applies the cooldown and the cost?

quiz.prompt: A programmer subtracts stamina in the ability and also applies a cost effect. What does the player feel?
choices: Stamina drops twice for one activation.
A shorter cooldown, because two costs finish faster.
No change. The effect deletes the hand subtract.
The ability cannot start, because effects block all activation.
quiz.why: One cost, in the effect.
quiz.review_prompt: A programmer subtracts stamina in the ability and also applies a cost effect. What does the player feel?

quiz.prompt: True or false: A gameplay effect applies cost and cooldown. Do not subtract the cost by hand as well.
choices: True
False
quiz.why: That is the lesson.
quiz.review_prompt: True or false: A gameplay effect applies cost and cooldown. Do not subtract the cost by hand as well.

quiz.prompt: True or false: Hand-subtracting the cost is required because effects only change visuals.
choices: True
False
quiz.why: Effects change attributes.
quiz.review_prompt: True or false: Hand-subtracting the cost is required because effects only change visuals.

quiz.prompt: A damage-over-time should tick how?
choices: As an effect the ability system applies, on its own period.
As a character Tick that subtracts health whenever a bool might be set.
As an OnRep that subtracts every time the value replicates.
As a line trace from the camera.
quiz.why: Duration and period belong to the effect.
quiz.review_prompt: A damage-over-time should tick how?

quiz.prompt: Who removes the effect when the stun ends?
choices: The ability system, when the effect expires or is removed.
The animator, by stopping the montage.
The owning machine, by writing the attribute back to full.
The overlap of the floor.
quiz.why: The system owns the effect lifetime.
quiz.review_prompt: Who removes the effect when the stun ends?

quiz.prompt: True or false: A cooldown effect can block a second activation without a parallel float named CooldownRemaining on the character.
choices: True
False
quiz.why: The effect is the cooldown.
quiz.review_prompt: True or false: A cooldown effect can block a second activation without a parallel float named CooldownRemaining on the character.

quiz.prompt: The HUD wants the remaining cooldown. What should it read?
choices: The effect or the attribute the system already exposes. It should not keep its own timer as the source of truth.
A timer it starts itself when it sees the button, ignoring the server. The widget would then own cooldown.
Tick's frame count.
The mesh material parameter, as the only stored duration.
quiz.why: Read the system. Do not invent a second clock.
quiz.review_prompt: The HUD wants the remaining cooldown. What should it read?

quiz.prompt: True or false: Applying the effect and also calling the old health subtract keeps both generations of the code correct.
choices: True
False
quiz.why: Both will run.
quiz.review_prompt: True or false: Applying the effect and also calling the old health subtract keeps both generations of the code correct.

quiz.prompt: A heal effect and a damage effect touch the same health attribute. What prevents a second secret float from ignoring one of them?
choices: There is no second float. Both effects modify the one attribute.
The character Tick rewrites health from the float after every effect.
The widget averages the float and the attribute.
OnRep copies the float back over the attribute.
quiz.why: One attribute, many effects.
quiz.review_prompt: A heal effect and a damage effect touch the same health attribute. What prevents a second secret float from ignoring one of them?

quiz.prompt: True or false: Effects are client-only cosmetics, so the authority should keep a hand-written subtract as the real cost.
choices: True
False
quiz.why: The effect is the real cost.
quiz.review_prompt: True or false: Effects are client-only cosmetics, so the authority should keep a hand-written subtract as the real cost.

quiz.prompt: What does the player notice if the cost effect is missing and only the montage plays?
choices: The ability looks like it ran
The montage refuses to play.
Health replicates as the montage length.
Input unbinds.
quiz.why: No effect, no cost.
